More than 10 reported hauntings reveal Leicestershire's 'most haunted' area

Reports range from phantom tobacco smoke and unexplained footsteps to poltergeist claims involving flying plates

14:01, 31 Oct 2026

A Leicestershire postcode with more than 10 reported 'hauntings' has been crowned the county's 'most haunted' area.

‌

‌

The data comes from author Dr Paul Lee, who has documented more than 5,500 reported hauntings around the country over a decade of research.

‌

The reports range from phantom tobacco smoke and unexplained footsteps to poltergeist claims involving flying plates and airborne kitchen utensils.

‌

In Leicestershire, the city centre has been crowned the 'most haunted' area, with 11 claims of paranormal experiences.

Tied in second place are Oadby and Market Harborough, with two reports of 'hauntings' in each area.

Paranormal experiences are then dotted around the county, with one-off reports being made in Glenfield, Rushey Mead, Cropston and Market Bosworth.

‌

In total, there have been more than 25 reports of paranormal activity across Leicestershire. You can discover the haunted locations near you using our interactive map.

‌

According to Dr Lee’s research, Britain’s most haunted postcode is the ME1 neighbourhood, which covers Rochester, Burham, and Wouldham in Kent.

Paranormal experiences have been documented at more than 50 separate locations across these Medway communities.

‌

Among them is the former Royal Function Rooms, an 18th-century theatre that closed in 2022. The venue was long said to be haunted by three separate spectres.

They include an aggressive figure in an 18th-century waistcoat who allegedly ran across the stage overturning furniture, a second shouting phantom, and a woman in a bonnet who was reported to rattle door handles in the basement.

‌

York city centre (YO1) is the UK’s second most haunted postcode, famous for its ghost walks. One of the city's most chilling tales centres on St Saviour Church, where a "grey lady" is reputed to walk at midnight.

Local folklore tells of an amateur ghost hunter who spent the night locked inside the church, only to be discovered the following morning either dead with his face a “mask of terror”, or scared out of his senses, depending on the retelling.

All the descriptions of paranormal activity on the map have come from Dr Lee’s research, which, in many cases, includes interviews with witnesses and his own investigations, during which he has visited numerous locations and studied various newspaper archives.

Dr Lee said: "Of course, some of the reports in the database could be hoaxes or urban legends; there is no way to know in many cases."
